unchanged_question_contract_assessment.reasoning: The literal question challenges a fixed polynomial in N,M alone for any stored matrix materialization when supplier work is unrestricted/data-dependent, and asks for a precise counterexample and exact condition. This has the uniform interpretation: one dimensions-only polynomial must cover the admitted supplier/input class. The candidate explicitly fixes that quantifier rather than silently imposing constant-time suppliers. substantive_reconstruction.counted_semantics: Cost is a function from eight operation tags to nonnegative natural counts. A charged add increments field by one, including add(z,0); Run.pure has cost zero and Run.bind adds ledgers. collect at length k retains the sum of supplier ledgers and adds k*(2read+2write). Applying collect inside collect gives, for every op, C(op)=S(op)+(NM+N)s(op), with S(op)=sum_i sum_j cost(f(i,j),op) and s=2read+2write. The outer N copies store/project row references, so they remain even when M=0.
substantive_reconstruction.concrete_counterexample_and_quantifiers: Define t_0=pure(0), t_(K+1)=t_K.bind(lambda z:add(z,0)). Induction gives value(t_K)=0 and cost(t_K)=K*tick(field); there are no other charged calls. At N=M=1 take the unique entry supplier constantly t_K. Thus its stored value is always the same 1-by-1 zero matrix, yet materialization has exactly K field operations and four reads plus four writes from (1+1)*s. For every proposed fixed polynomial p bounding field cost uniformly over all suppliers, its value p(1,1) is finite, so choose a natural K>p(1,1); the total field cost exceeds it. This is a family of concrete finite terminating counted computations, not an assertion that one finite computation has infinite cost. If the intended class consists of data-parameterized computations, one family taking unbounded K as input gives the same fixed-dimension obstruction. The argument does not require infinite loops, uncounted scalar arithmetic, growing dimensions or changed returned values.
substantive_reconstruction.exact_condition: For any specified supplier/input class and any counter op, S(op)<=C(op) by nonnegativity. Hence existence of one polynomial upper bound uniform in that class for C implies such a bound for S. Conversely, if S(op)<=P_op(N,M) uniformly for a fixed polynomial P_op, then C(op)<=P_op(N,M)+(NM+N)s(op), again a polynomial. Eight tags are finite, so counterwise uniform polynomial bounds and a uniform polynomial total bound imply one another by finite summation/domination. The exact obstruction is absence of a uniform bound on aggregate counted supplier work, not nonconstancy of individual costs. A uniform per-entry bound B_op(N,M) with polynomial control gives S<=NM*B_op and is a useful sufficient interface; an uncontrolled external parameter B is only conditional, not dimensions-only complexity.
substantive_reconstruction.necessity_of_repair: The predecessor's j-additions example has aggregate N*M*(M-1)/2, already a polynomial in dimensions. It does not defeat existence of some polynomial upper bound; different costs at equal dimensions can also lie below a single bound. Its unrestricted B claim omitted the need to control B in dimensions. The successor supplies the missing universal-over-suppliers quantifier and a witness for each proposed p, and states the exact aggregate condition instead of falsely calling a constant per-entry premise necessary.
substantive_reconstruction.empty_and_resource_boundaries: If N=0, both S and NM+N vanish and materialization costs zero. If M=0 with N>0, no entry supplier is called, S=0, but the N row-reference surcharge remains. Thus positive dimensions in the counterexample are essential and supplied. No rank, matrix norm, nonzero entry or state-normalization promise is needed. The charged primitive loop is a valid construction within the source model, not an asserted existing named Lean theorem. Proof checking, counter/loop bookkeeping and finite-bit representations are outside the declared model.
